text:
maria: Heads-up — after the runtime + model swap in canary this morning (split-attn-light + q3a quant profile) we're seeing an unexpected drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the LLM serving pool. Before: ~89% steady, after: ~62% and warmup tails at 5m are much worse.

raj: ack. do we know which kernel variant triggered this? split-attn-light was rolled behind the kernel-selection flag, right?

maria: yes flag=opt.split_attn_light=true on canary nodes. kernel-selection logs show a mix of legacy and new kernels depending on seq len bin. I dug traces: requests with early short prefixes (<=32) are the worst hit-rate losers.

dennis: can you paste perf counters / profiler snapshot? even a tiny trace helps.

maria: here's a capture from a 10-min window on node-07: 
```
PrefixCache: total_lookups=184k, hits=114k, hit_rate=0.619
KVCache: collision_retries=12, avg_key_len=72
Batching: avg_microbatch_size=3.2, alignment_misses=18%
KernelSelect: split_attn_light=enabled(42%), fused_attn_v2=enabled(58%)
P50_latency=41ms, P95_latency=190ms, cold_warmup_spike=+420ms
```

anya: interesting — alignment_misses 18% stands out. microbatch alignment can break key normalization if we changed how prefix fingerprint is computed across microbatches. any code paths that touched key canonicalization?

maria: yes, the compiler change moved a `pad_normalize()` call from prefetch -> postprefetch for performance, so padding tokens are now visible in the kernel fingerprint step. that could salt keys inconsistently across batching.

raj: that matches: if padding moves into fingerprint window, same logical prefix can hash differently depending on batch packing. That would reduce effective hit-rate without evictions.

ci-bot: deploy job #3789 finished on canary nodes: 2026-03-18T09:12:00Z (split-attn-light + q3a).

dennis: repro idea: run synthetic generator with deterministic prefixes and vary microbatch packing (pack=dynamic vs pack=fixed) and compare prefix fingerprints. if pad_normalize moved, dynamic packing will flip bits.

maria: I'm running quick repro now — initial results look promising: with pad_normalize prefetch we get 91% hit, with postprefetch we get 64%.

anya: can you snapshot key fingerprints for the same request under both code paths? we need a diff to show canonicalization break.

maria: attaching snippet from fingerprint dump (truncated):
```
req_id=abc123 pack=dynamic fingerprint_old=0x7a3f2c9b fingerprint_new=0x1c9b4f2a
req_id=def456 pack=fixed   fingerprint_old=0x4d9a1120 fingerprint_new=0x4d9a1120
req_id=ghi789 pack=dynamic fingerprint_old=0x2f33a001 fingerprint_new=0x8c33a001
```

raj: perfect — that shows deterministic divergence only when packing changes. so the regression is key normalization ordering + kernel compiler reorder.

dennis: mitigation options: 1) hotfix to move pad_normalize back to prefetch (low-risk rollback), 2) make fingerprint function padding-agnostic (more involved), 3) force fixed packing for now (workaround).

anya: what about interaction with quant profile q3a? could rounding/quant noise amplify mismatch?

maria: q3a mostly affects compute kernels; it doesn't change the logical token sequence. but quant path did change a micro-op that reduced some zeroing ops — that may have made the old prefetch-noise assumption brittle. basically two orthogonal changes combined.

raj: recommended immediate plan: rollback pad_normalize position on canary (hotfix), run repro harness across seq bins, validate hit-rate back to baseline, then schedule a small refactor to make fingerprint canonical independent of packing. assign owners?

maria: I'll open a PR for the rollback and the repro job. Dennis can you own the fingerprint refactor?

dennis: yep, I'll take the refactor. will add unit tests for pack=fixed/dynamic and seq trim.

anya: also add a perf job that measures aligned microbatch hit-rate delta across kernel variants. we should catch this in CI.

ci-bot: job #3790 started: canary rollback test matrix (pack=dynamic,fixed x kernels=split_attn_light,fused_attn_v2).

maria: thanks all. I'll post follow-up when canary metrics show recovery. :white_check_mark:
